monsters.name: Aboleth
monsters.pageRef: Aboleth [Monster Manual, page 8, Expanded Psionics Handbook, page 185]

description.text: A hulking amphibious predator of lightless underground water, heavy through the body and smooth as an eel, with three stacked eyes and four long tentacles that it drags itself along on when it leaves the shallows. It thinks in inherited memory older than most civilisations, speaks mind to mind, and regards the surface and everyone on it as livestock.

attacks.name: Sharp Teeth
attacks.notes: Sharp Teeth (11): thrust 1d cutting (KYOS: 2d+2 cutting), Reach C.

attacks.name: Tentacle
attacks.notes: Tentacle (11): thrust 3d-1 crushing (KYOS: 5d+1 crushing), Reach C-3.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (11): thrust 4d-1 crushing (KYOS: 7d crushing), Reach C-2. Can only attack rear hexes. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Mucus Cloud
attacks.notes: When underwater, the aboleth exudes a mucus cloud. Any creature in the same hex as the aboleth that breathes in the mucus must make a successful HT roll or lose the ability to breathe air and gain that ability to breathe water for 30 minutes times the margin of failure.

traits: Dependency (Water; Constantly; Enters hibernation after losing 1xHP)
Extra Legs (Four Legs; Cannot Kick; Extra-Flexible; Long 1)
Likes eating victims transformed by slime
Weakness (Immersion in saline water, 1d per 30 minutes)

description.text: A flightless bird the size of a warhorse, walking on four stiff obsidian legs with a compact armoured body slung between them. It keeps to burnt, sulfur-smelling country where organised cruelty is ordinary, kills with a hooked beak and heavy claws, and takes its time about it.

attacks.name: Sharp Beak
attacks.notes: Sharp Beak (14): thrust 2d+1 large piercing (KYOS: 3d+3 large piercing), Reach C.

attacks.name: Sharp Claws
attacks.notes: Sharp Claws (14): thrust 2d+1 cutting (KYOS: 3d+3 cutting), Reach C-1.

attacks.name: Black Cloud
attacks.notes: By spending 2 FP and performing a Ready maneuver, an achaierai can release a choking, toxic black cloud. It spreads in a 2-yard radius area around the achaierai, lasts 10 seconds, and drifts with the wind. The cloud imposes a -3 penalty on all vision- and Infravision-based rolls within the area. Additionally, every creature that inhales the cloud must make an HT roll. If it fails, it takes 1d toxic damage, ignoring DR, and begins to hallucinate for margin of failure minutes. After that the subject is stunned (p. B420) and may roll vs. HT once per second to recover. Achaierais are immune to this ability.

traits: Regeneration (Slow; Accessibility, Only legs and feet)

description.text: What is left of someone who died insane: a tattered upper body trailing away into smoke, no legs beneath it, hands drawn out too long. It cannot form words, only a rising babble that scatters thought, and its touch leaves the living hallucinating. Religious symbols drive it back.

attacks.name: Punch
attacks.notes: Punch (11): thrust 1d-4 crushing (KYOS: 1d-5 crushing), Reach C. Only against insubstantial targets.

attacks.name: Touch of Insanity
attacks.notes: Despite being insubstantial, allips can cause temporary insanity with their touch. Any living creature that touches an allip must make a Will roll (Mind Shield provides a bonus to resist, but DR does not) or begin to hallucinate for margin of failure minutes.

attacks.name: Babble
attacks.notes: When a creature hears the allip’s constant babble, it must roll a Fright Check using the Confusion table (GURPS Powers, p. 85). If a victim succeeds at his Fright Check, he will be unaffected by this ability for one hour.

attacks.name: Madness
attacks.notes: When a creature reads the mind of an allip or senses its emotions – by any method, including powers, spells, and unmodified advantages, it must roll a Fright Check. If a victim succeeds at his Fright Check, he will be unaffected by this ability for one hour.

description.text: A six-legged burrowing arthropod as heavy as a pony, with shovel-like foreclaws and mandibles that run with digestive acid. Nearly blind and completely deaf, it hunts by the tremor of footsteps overhead, erupting out of tilled soil to seize whatever is passing and drag it under.

attacks.name: Sharp Claws

attacks.name: Spit Acid

description.text: A feathered, legless hunter of the open air, built like a barbed dart with a hooked beak at the front and a rudder of a tail behind. It never lands willingly, spits arcs of lightning at range, and treats anything sharing its sky as an intruder to be driven off.

attacks.name: Sharp Beak
attacks.notes: Sharp Beak (15): thrust 1d-1 large piercing (KYOS: 1d-4 large piercing), Reach C.

attacks.name: Electricity Ray
attacks.damage: The arrowhawk fires forth a coruscating beam of electricity from its tail that does 2d burning surge damage. The attack has Acc 3 and Range 20/100. Metallic armor counts as DR 1 against this attack, but nonmetallic armor protects normally. Targets stuck by this attack must make an HT roll, at -1 per 2 points of injury, or be physically stunned. On subsequent turns, they can roll HT to recover. The charge of electricity can be dodged, but not blocked or parried. This attack behaves unpredictably around conductors; see Lightning (GURPS Magic, p. 196) for more details

description.text: A sphere of steady white-gold light no bigger than a helm, with no body to speak of: no face, no limbs, nothing an ordinary weapon can find. It drifts rather than walks, answers questions honestly and at some length, and fights fiends with lances of focused light while refusing to harm anyone innocent.

attacks.name: Light Ray
attacks.damage: 1d tight-beam burning. Ranged attack (Acc 3, Range 10). Costs 1 FP per use. Cannot affect holy beings. The beam is easily reflected. Normally it cannot be blocked, but someone may use a mirror or a highly polished shield to do so; this causes the attack to bounce off in a random direction, possibly striking the wrong target (p. B389). The mirror-wielder may even attempt to reflect it back at the archon, but this gives -2 to Block; the archon defends normally. On the upside, the archon may make use of mirrored surfaces to “ricochet” the beam. This inflicts -2 per bounce to the attack roll, but may allow the attacker to bypass cover; in addition, the target is at -1 per bounce to defend

description.text: A thick braided creeper with muscular tendrils, black recurved thorns and pale bell-shaped flowers, lying among ordinary undergrowth it cannot be told apart from. Blind and deaf, it waits for weight and warmth to pass within reach, then wraps and squeezes until whatever it caught stops moving and rots into the soil beneath it.

attacks.name: Entangle (Binding 10)
attacks.notes: No attack roll. Emanation covering an 8-yard radius, usable only where the area holds dense vegetation. Victims caught in the area are bound at effective ST 10 and stay bound for roughly 100 seconds; escape is a Quick Contest against the Binding's ST. Persistent, so the binding is not consumed by one escape.

description.text: A low, heavy lizard about as long as a man is tall, running on eight short legs, rough-scaled in olive and ochre with a blunt wedge of a head. It is slow, ill-tempered and entirely unhurried, because it has no need of speed: whatever meets its glowing amber eyes stops being flesh.

attacks.name: Sharp Teeth
attacks.notes: Sharp Teeth (10): thrust 1d+1 cutting (KYOS: 2d cutting), Reach C.

attacks.name: Petrifying Gaze
attacks.damage: A basilisk’s petrifying gaze spreads out in a cone 15 yards long and 15 yards wide at the end. It can select who is affected; potential victims must be looking at it. For every target, there is a Quick Contest between the basilisk’s Will (minus a range penalty taken from the Speed/Range Table) and each target’s HT. If the basilisk wins, the target is petrified. (The distinction between “paralyzed” and “petrified” generally works in their victims’ favor – e.g., they won’t starve – so the basilisk does not pay extra for this.) Someone looking at a reflection of a basilisk is not affected by its gaze. Fighting while looking in a mirror is at a -5 penalty; attacks made with closed eyes are at -10. Petrification can be removed with Remove Curse or Stone to Flesh. This attack also affects insubstantial beings

description.text: A lean, scarred figure in an iron half-mask, wearing a mantle of interlocked black chain that does not hang the way metal should. The chains move at its will, striking from angles no arm could reach, and it holds a victim's gaze while they do. It heals what you cut, and it is in no hurry.

attacks.name: Punch
attacks.notes: Punch (11): thrust 1d crushing (KYOS: 1d+2 crushing), Reach C. The damage includes the +1 bonus for improvised brass knuckles.

attacks.name: Chains
attacks.damage: The chain devil has two long chains that it can use to attack enemies. These chains deal swing 2d crushing
attacks.notes: Chains (15): The chain devil has two long chains that it can use to attack enemies. These chains deal swing 2d crushing, Reach 1-4*. The chains are awkward enough that they require a Ready maneuver to change reach (e.g., between 1 and 3). Otherwise, the chain devil can strike at foes that are at any distance within the chains’ reach. Attempts to parry the chains are at -4, and fencing weapons cannot parry at all! Attempts to block chains are at -2. This swinging attack is unbalanced – the chain devil cannot use it to parry if it has already used it to attack this turn (or vice versa), and parries with the chains are at -2. The chain devil has two chain attacks, which permits him Dual-Weapon Attacks (p. B417). The chains have DR 4 and effective weight 1.4 lbs. This attack uses the Kusari skill.

attacks.name: Dancing Chains
attacks.damage: The chain devil can animate any chain within 10 yards of him. He can animate up to 8 yards of chain, assuming the chain weighs 2 lbs. per yard. 8 yards of chain have 20 HP. An animated chain can grab, lift, strike, and throw with ST equal to its HP/2. It has the chain devil’s DX. It can walk and jump if it isn’t fixed in place; Move equals 10–HP/2. The chain devil can use skills through animated chains (including Kusari to make swinging attacks) – but note that chains have No Fine Manipulators. Chains return to their rest state once the chain devil gives up control
attacks.notes: Dancing Chains (15): The chain devil can animate any chain within 10 yards of him. He can animate up to 8 yards of chain, assuming the chain weighs 2 lbs. per yard. 8 yards of chain have 20 HP. An animated chain can grab, lift, strike, and throw with ST equal to its HP/2. It has the chain devil’s DX. It can walk and jump if it isn’t fixed in place; Move equals 10–HP/2. The chain devil can use skills through animated chains (including Kusari to make swinging attacks) – but note that chains have No Fine Manipulators. Chains return to their rest state once the chain devil gives up control.

description.text: A headless, legless mass that slithers on a broad tapered underside and does not hold any shape long enough to describe twice. Limbs and claws surface where it needs them. Transformation magic slides off something already refusing to have a form, and its touch leaves a body unsure what shape it is meant to be.

attacks.name: Sharp Claws
attacks.notes: Sharp Claws (12): thrust 1d+1 cutting (KYOS: 2d cutting), Reach C. If a living takes damage from the chaos beast’s claws, it must make a HT check to resist a transformative effect. Its body transforms into an amorphous mass for margin of failure minutes. Its Basic Move is reduced by 2, it gains Injury Tolerance (Homogenous, No Blood, No Head, No Neck), Invertebrate, Mute, No Legs (Slithers), and No Manipulators. It cannot wear any armor or use any items in this state - they all become useless and fall from the victim’s body. In addition, the victim constantly experiences terrible pain (p. B428). The victim can negate this effect and return to its natural form by taking a Concentrate maneuver a making a successful Will-4 roll. If successful, he retains his shape until the end of his next turn.

traits: Injury Tolerance (Homogenous, No Blood, No Head, No Neck)

description.text: A broad rust-red crustacean on four walking legs, with two heavy pincer arms, visible gill fans and a blunt eyeless head fused into the carapace. Below the head hang four short pale tentacles whose touch leaves a body limp and aware. It senses the water and air around it well enough not to miss the lack of eyes.

attacks.name: Pincers
attacks.notes: Pincers (12): thrust 2d+2 cutting (KYOS: 4d-1 cutting), Reach C-1. The chuul can either nip and let go or hold on and grapple the victim in addition to injuring him. Either is an attack that takes full hit location penalties – not halved for grappling. Treat this attack as a bite for these purposes (see Teeth on page 115 of GURPS Martial Arts for details). The pincers give +2 with tasks that require a firm grip (including climbing).

attacks.name: Weak Bite
attacks.notes: Weak Bite (12): thrust 1d+2 crushing, Reach C.

attacks.name: Paralytic Tentacles
attacks.damage: A chuul can lash out with its tentacles to paralyze his victim. This attack has Reach C and cannot parry. If the tentacle touches bare skin, the victim must roll HT to resist. He becomes paralyzed for 3 seconds per point of margin of failure. After that the subject is stunned (p. B420) and may roll vs. HT once per second to recover

description.text: A scorpion of volcanic basalt colouring seamed with sulfur yellow, big enough to straddle a road, with iron-black pincers and an ivory sting arched far above the ground. There is nothing subtle about it and nothing local that can fight it. It simply walks in and eats.

Poison: Toxic Attack 1d (Cyclic, 1 hour, 5 cycles, Resistible, +50%; Follow-Up, Sting, +0%; Resistible, HT-4, -10%; Symptoms, 2/3 HP, -3 HT and -5 DX, +65%) Resolve as stated by the construction; the source gives no separate resolution text.

attacks.name: Pincers
attacks.notes: Pincers (14): thrust 7d cutting (KYOS: 7d+2 cutting), Reach C-3. The monstrous scorpion can either nip and let go or hold on and grapple the victim in addition to injuring him. Either is an attack that takes full hit location penalties – not halved for grappling. Treat this attack as a bite for these purposes (see Teeth on page 115 of GURPS Martial Arts for details). The pincers give +2 with tasks that require a firm grip (including climbing).

description.text: A ridiculous-looking bird the size of a large goose: rooster's head and crimson comb on a compact feathered body, two clawed legs, two small wings, and a long green-black serpent's tail. Nothing about it is dangerous except the beak, and the beak turns whatever it breaks the skin of to stone.

attacks.name: Petrification
attacks.notes: With a Ready maneuver, a cockatrice can activate its petrification ability. Any creature that touches the cockatrice, even insubstantial or ethereal creatures, must make an HT roll to resist. If it fails, then the creature becomes permanently petrified. This effect cannot be dispelled by Dispel Magic, but can be negated by Remove Curse or Stone to Flesh. This ability stays on until the cockatrice turns it off with a Ready maneuver, and it works even if it is stunned, unconscious, or asleep, but not dead (however, the tail feathers retain this ability 1d days after death). Cockatrices are immune to this petrification ability, but not to other petrification effects.

description.text: A long serpent in turquoise and gold with two vast feathered wings and a horn-crested head. It is old, genuinely wise, and considerably more intelligent than most of what it speaks to. It coils and constricts when it must fight, but it would far rather talk, and it usually gets what it wants that way.

attacks.name: Fangs
attacks.damage: thrust 2d+2 impaling (KYOS: 5d-1 impaling) plus follow-up 1d-1 toxic (resisted by HT-3, 2 1-hour cycles, -3 ST after losing 1/3 HP, -4 ST after losing 2/3 HP)
attacks.notes: Fangs (16): thrust 2d+2 impaling (KYOS: 5d-1 impaling) plus follow-up 1d-1 toxic (resisted by HT-3, 2 1-hour cycles, -3 ST after losing 1/3 HP, -4 ST after losing 2/3 HP), Reach C.

attacks.name: Sun Awe
attacks.notes: With a Ready maneuver, the couatl in direct sunlight can spread its rainbow-colored wings to create awe-inspiring patterns. When a creature sees these patterns, it must roll a Fright Check at a -3 penalty using the Awe variant table (GURPS Powers, p. 85). If a victim succeeds at his Fright Check, he will be unaffected by this ability for one hour.

Nondetection: The couatl is nearly impossible to detect, see, or divine with any Information spells, regardless of the magic system used to cast them. Reduce the diviner’s effective margin of success by 10 for these purposes – so a spell that succeeded by 0-9 completely fails to find the couatl, while one that succeeded by 10+ provides less information than normal and is at a huge disadvantage if it’s resisted.

Poison (follow-up on Bite): Toxic Attack 1d-1 (Cyclic, 1 hour, 2 cycles, Resistible, +20%; Follow-Up, Bite, +0%; Resistible, HT-3, -15%; Symptoms, 1/3 HP, -3 ST, +45%; Symptoms, 2/3 HP, -4 ST, +20%) Resolve as stated by the construction; the source gives no separate resolution text.

attacks.notes: Once every 15 seconds the vrock can emit a 2-yard radius cloud of spores around himself. This requires a Concentrate maneuver and costs 1 FP. The spores work as a contact agent, ignoring unsealed DR and dealing 1 point of toxic damage every 10 seconds for 6 cycles total. At the end of this time, the victim is covered with a tangle of viny growths. The vines are harmless and wither away in 1d4 days. The spores can be removed with a successful Physician roll (takes 10 seconds). Bless, neutralize poison, or remove disease kills the spores, as does sprinkling the victim with a vial of holy water.

attacks.name: Dance of Ruin
attacks.notes: To use this ability, a group of at least three vrocks must join hands in a circle, dancing wildly and chanting. At the end of 16 seconds of dancing, a wave of crackling energy flashes outward in a 32-yard radius. All creatures except for demons within the radius take 6d crushing damage. This affects even insubstantial creatures. Stunning, paralyzing, or slaying one of the vrocks stops the dance. The dance costs each vrock 2 FP.

attacks.name: Entangle
attacks.damage: Each erinyes carries a stout rope some 50 feet long that entangles anyone it strikes. The erinyes uses Whip skill for this attack. It is treated as a melee attack with a range equal to the rope’s length, but not more than 20 yards. On a hit, the victim is grappled (see p. B370) and rooted in place. He cannot select the Move or Change Posture maneuvers or change facing, and is at -4 to DX. The ST of this effect is equal to 10. To break free, the victim must win a Quick Contest of ST or Escape skill against 10. Each attempt takes one second. If the victim fails to break free, he loses 1 FP but may try again. Alternatively, he may try to destroy the rope. Innate Attacks hit automatically; other attacks are at -4. External attacks on the rope take no penalty, but risk hitting the victim on a miss (see Striking Into a Close Combat, p. B392). The rope has DR 3. Each point of damage reduces ST by one. At ST 0, the rope is destroyed and the victim is freed

attacks.name: Spiked Chains
attacks.damage: The zelekhut can take a Ready maneuver to unfurl spiked chains from his forearms or to retract them back. These chains deal swing 2d crushing
attacks.notes: Spiked Chains (16): The zelekhut can take a Ready maneuver to unfurl spiked chains from his forearms or to retract them back. These chains deal swing 2d crushing, Reach 1-4*. The chains are awkward enough that they require a Ready maneuver to change reach (e.g., between 1 and 3). Otherwise, the zelekhut can strike at foes that are at any distance within the chains’ reach. Attempts to parry the chains are at -4, and fencing weapons cannot parry at all! Attempts to block chains are at -2. This swinging attack is unbalanced – the zelekhut cannot use it to parry if he have already used it to attack this turn (or vice versa), and parries with the chains are at -2. The zelekhut has two chain attacks, which permits him Dual-Weapon Attacks (p. B417). Spikes favor disarming, giving the zelekhut a +2 on disarming attempts. The chains have DR 4 and effective weight 0.84 lbs. This attack uses the Kusari skill.

description.text: A shapeless mass of viscous black matter that pours along walls and ceilings as easily as floors, and weighs several tons. It is blind, mindless and entirely without organs, so there is nothing on it to aim at; what it flows over, it digests.

attacks.name: Engulf (Binding ST 24)
attacks.notes: No attack roll is necessary; the quarry may defend only by dodging and retreating. Moving through an SM+2 or smaller creature is an automatic slam. A victim who fails to dodge is pinned if smaller than the pudding, or grappled if equal or larger. Breaking free is a Quick Contest of ST (only every 10 seconds if pinned; on a 17 or 18 the victim cannot escape unaided); the pudding has +10 ST when pinning and +5 when grappling. Engulfed victims cannot breathe and begin to suffocate when out of breath. It can pin or grapple one foe at a time; others are pushed along in front of it unless they win a Quick Contest of ST. It may constrict an engulfed victim every turn at effective ST 24.

attacks.name: Acid (Corrosion Aura)
attacks.notes: Always on, no attack roll. Any organic or metal creature or object touching the pudding takes 1d-1 corrosion per second; stone is unaffected. Engulfed creatures and objects take it as large-area injury. Selective, so it does not destroy what the pudding is not attacking.

description.text: A transparent cube of dense jelly, wider than the corridor it fills and nearly invisible until light catches an edge. It sweeps passages at a walking pace, digesting everything organic it engulfs and carrying the indigestible — coins, buckles, blades — suspended inside it as it goes.

attacks.name: Engulf (Binding ST 30)
attacks.notes: No attack roll is necessary; the quarry may defend only by dodging and retreating. Moving through an SM+1 or smaller creature is an automatic slam. A victim who fails to dodge is pinned if smaller than the cube, or partly stuck and grappled if equal or larger. Breaking free is a Quick Contest of ST (only every 10 seconds if pinned; on a 17 or 18 the victim cannot escape unaided); the cube has +10 ST when pinning and +5 when grappling. Engulfed victims cannot breathe and begin to suffocate when out of breath. It may constrict an engulfed victim every turn at effective ST 30.

attacks.name: Acid (Corrosion Aura)
attacks.notes: Always on, no attack roll. Any organic creature or object touching the cube takes 1d-1 corrosion per second; stone and metal are unaffected, which is why cubes carry undigested treasure. Engulfed creatures and objects take it as large-area injury. Selective.

attacks.name: Paralysis (Affliction 1, HT)
attacks.notes: Contact agent, always on, no attack roll. Bare skin touching the cube must roll against HT or be paralysed for 3 seconds per point of margin of failure, then stunned with a HT roll once per second to recover. Underwater the slime is diluted and victims resist at +3.

traits: Injury Tolerance (Homogenous, No Blood, No Eyes, No Head, No Neck)

attacks.name: Sharp Teeth

attacks.damage: See GURPS Powers: Enhanced Senses, p. 17
attacks.notes: Passive Electroreception (12): See GURPS Powers: Enhanced Senses, p. 17.

attacks.name: Stunning Shock
attacks.damage: Once per 5 seconds, the shocker lizard can create an electrical discharge that has a chance to stun an enemy. This is a ranged attack with 1/2D 10, Max 100, Acc 3, RoF 1, Shots N/A, and Recoil 1. It works at 1/10 of its range underwater. A struck victim must make an immediate HT roll with a bonus equal to half of his DR. The victim gets a further +3 if he is beyond 1/2D range. If the victim makes his HT roll, he is unaffected. If he fails, he is stunned (see p. B420). He may roll vs. HT once per second to recover (DR has no effect on this roll)
attacks.notes: Stunning Shock (14): Once per 5 seconds, the shocker lizard can create an electrical discharge that has a chance to stun an enemy. attacks.name: Lethal Shock
attacks.notes: Once per 5 seconds, whenever a shocker lizard has two other shocker lizards within 4 yards, it can create a lethal shock in a 4-yard-radius area around itself. This shock deals 2d burning surge damage and can work underwater. Targets stuck by this attack must make an HT roll, at -1 per 2 points of penetrating damage, or be physically stunned. On subsequent turns, they can roll HT to recover.

description.text: A wasp-bodied hunter the size of a horse with heavy mandibles and a long sting, oily enough that a web cannot hold it. It hunts giant spiders specifically, paralyses one, and lays an egg in it for the larva to eat its way out of later.

attacks.name: Mandibles
attacks.notes: Mandibles (14): thrust 2d cutting (KYOS: 3d+2 cutting), Reach C.

attacks.name: Implant
attacks.notes: Female spider eaters lay their eggs inside paralyzed creatures of SM+2 or bigger. The eggs gestate for six weeks, then the host takes 2d toxic damage each hour for 13 cycles. This damage cannot be resisted. Once the host loses 1/2 of their HP to this effect, they begin experiencing terrible pain (p. B428) until they heal above that threshold. Once the host loses 2/3 of their HP to this effect, they begin experiencing agony (p. B428) until they heal above that threshold. The eggs can be removed with a successful Surgery roll (failure deals 1d-1 injury), or a Cure Disease spell cast at a -5 penalty. If the host dies to this effect, the young emerges, literally devouring the host from inside.

attacks.name: Fiddle
attacks.notes: A grig typically carries a tiny, grig-sized fiddle. When the grig plays the fiddle, all non-sprite creatures within 8 yards that hear the tune become overcome with the desire to dance for margin of failure minutes, if they fail to resist in a Quick Contest of the grig’s Musical Instrument (Fiddle) skill against their Will. This effect makes it very hard for the subject to do anything other than caper and prance in place. The subject can move at half of his Move, defends at -4, and is at -4 to DX and IQ. description.text: A rust-red flying thing the size of a cat, all wings and clutching legs around a long needle proboscis. It fastens on, drives the needle home and drinks until it is full or killed. One is a nuisance; they never come as one.

attacks.name: Proboscis
attacks.notes: Proboscis (15): thrust 1d-5 large piercing (KYOS: 1d-9 large piercing), Reach C. The stirge can drain the victim’s life if the victim is helpless (pinned, stunned, unconscious, etc.), grappled, or willing. If he is wearing armor, the stirge’s proboscis damage must penetrate its DR. Once the stirge has bitten through the victim’s DR, it can drain 1 HP per second from him. For every 3 HP stolen, the stirge heals 1 HP or 1 FP (his choice). It cannot raise his HP or FP above normal this way.

attacks.name: Attach
attacks.damage: The pincers are not very strong, but the stirge has four of them. Wrestling at DX+1 gives the stirge a ST score of 4 for the purpose of grappling. Effective skill 18 includes a +4 bonus for using 4 pincers at once
attacks.notes: Attach (18): The pincers are not very strong, but the stirge has four of them. Wrestling at DX+1 gives the stirge a ST score of 4 for the purpose of grappling. description.text: A shelled sea creature the size of a large dog, with pincer arms and a hard case pierced by openings it shifts its limbs between. It sees in every direction at once, swims fast, and squirts a blinding ink before it decides whether to fight.

attacks.name: Pincers
attacks.notes: Pincers (13): thrust 1d-3 cutting (KYOS: 1d-4 cutting), Reach C. The tojanida can either nip and let go or hold on and grapple the victim in addition to injuring him. Either is an attack that takes full hit location penalties – not halved for grappling. Treat this attack as a bite for these purposes (see Teeth on page 115 of GURPS Martial Arts for details). The pincers give +2 with tasks that require a firm grip (including climbing).

attacks.name: Sharp Teeth
attacks.notes: Sharp Teeth (13): thrust 1d-3 cutting (KYOS: 1d-4 cutting), Reach C.

attacks.name: Ink
attacks.damage: A tojanida may fill a two-yard-radius area with black ink. No one can see into the affected area, and no one within the affected area can see anything; see p. B394 for combat rules. In addition, this ink cloud imposes a -4 penalty on Smell rolls. Once created, the cloud persists for 10 seconds, drifting with the current. This cloud can only be used in water or in zero-G. When used on land, this attack takes a form of an ink jet, which can strike any target up to 20 yards away (without range or speed penalties). It can be dodged or blocked, but not parried. If the jet strikes the face, it causes no injury, but blinds the target for 3 seconds unless he makes a successful HT roll. Thick goggles, closed helmets, ultra-tech visors protect against this spell. A tojanida can use this ability only 4 times per day

description.text: The pale, hollow thing left when a vampire feeds without finishing: fanged, cold, casting no reflection, and bound to the will of whatever made it. It climbs sheer walls, closes its own wounds, and cannot cross the thresholds its master's rules forbid.

attacks.name: Punch
attacks.notes: Punch (15): thrust 1d crushing (KYOS: 1d+1 crushing), Reach C.

attacks.name: Vampiric Bite
attacks.notes: Vampiric Bite (15): thrust 1d cutting (KYOS: 1d+1 cutting), Reach C. The vampire can drain the victim’s life if the victim is helpless (pinned, stunned, unconscious, etc.), grappled, or willing. If he is wearing armor, the vampire’s biting damage must penetrate its DR. Once the vampire has bitten through the victim’s DR, he can drain 1 HP per second from him. For every 3 HP stolen, the vampire heals 1 HP or 1 FP (his choice). He cannot raise his HP or FP above normal this way.

description.text: A severed head the size of a melon with leathery bat wings where the ears should be and a mouth of green teeth, flapping through the dark. Its shriek freezes a victim in place, and its kiss begins turning that victim into another one of it.

attacks.name: Sharp Teeth
attacks.damage: thrust 1d-5 cutting (KYOS: 1d-9 cutting) + follow-up 1 toxic (3 1-hour cycles; Resisted with HT)
attacks.notes: Sharp Teeth (13): thrust 1d-5 cutting (KYOS: 1d-9 cutting) + follow-up 1 toxic (3 1-hour cycles; Resisted with HT), Reach C. Poison: Toxic Attack 1 (Cyclic, 1 hour, 3 cycles, Resistible, +20%; Follow-Up, Sharp Teeth, +0%; Resistible, HT, -35%) Resolve as stated by the construction; the source gives no separate resolution text.

attacks.name: Kiss
attacks.damage: A vargouille can kiss a target by making a successful unarmed attack against the target’s unprotected face. An affected opponent must succeed on a HT roll or begin a terrible transformation that turns the creature into a vargouille within 24 hours (and often much sooner; roll 1d separately for each phase of the transformation). First, over a period of 1d hours, all the victim’s hair falls out. Within another 1d hours thereafter, the ears grow into leathery wings, tentacles sprout on the chin and scalp, and the teeth become long, pointed fangs. During the next 1d hours, the victim takes loses 1 IQ each hour (maximum 3). The transformation is complete 1d hours later, when the subject experiences a heart attack and, if not resuscitated, the head breaks free of the body (which promptly dies) and becomes a vargouille. This transformation is interrupted by sunlight (it can delay death), but to reverse the transformation requires Cure Disease at -3 or Remove Curse. Dispel Magic will not lift this effect

description.text: A withered corpse with glowing eyes that keeps the bearing and bad temper of whoever it was, and prefers not to leave its own tomb. It knows where the living are without looking, and what its claws take from a person does not come back with rest.

attacks.name: Sharp Claws
attacks.notes: Sharp Claws (14): thrust 1d-1 cutting (KYOS: 1d cutting), Reach C.

attacks.name: Life Sense
attacks.damage: A wight possesses a constantly active magical ability to sense life. By making a Sense roll with normal range penalties, a wight may sense all nearby living beings, knowing their precise location. A follow-up IQ roll may reveal information about the living being, with margin of success of 0-1 only revealing vague information, such as race, and margin of success of 4+ revealing detailed information, such as age, gender, and physical condition
attacks.notes: Life Sense (10): A wight possesses a constantly active magical ability to sense life. By making a Sense roll with normal range penalties, a wight may sense all nearby living beings, knowing their precise location. A follow-up IQ roll may reveal information about the living being, with margin of success of 0-1 only revealing vague information, such as race, and margin of success of 4+ revealing detailed information, such as age, gender, and physical condition.

attacks.name: Psychic Value Sense
attacks.damage: Whenever a wight touches an object, the GM may make a roll against IQ-4 (6) to sense strong emotions and psychic impressions tied to the object’s history. On a critical success, the wight receives an actual vision of a significant past event. Roll at no additional penalty for events earlier the same day, at ‑1 for up to 10 days ago, ‑2 for up to 100 days ago, ‑3 for up to three years ago, and an another ‑1 per additional 10x multiplier. The wight cannot use this ability actively – this is a passive sense

description.text: A sea-dwelling elf with fine silver-green skin, webbed hands and gills, carrying a short spear and a dagger. Aquatic elves keep to coastal shallows and reefs, live a long time, and grow ill and weak if kept out of the water.

attacks.name: Short Spear (on land)
attacks.notes: Short Spear (on land) (13): thrust 1d-1 impaling, Reach 1.

attacks.name: Short Spear (underwater)
attacks.notes: Short Spear (underwater) (11): thrust 1d-2 impaling, Reach 1.

attacks.name: Dagger
attacks.notes: Dagger (13): thrust 1d-3 impaling, Reach C.

traits: Weakness (Immersion in fresh water, 1d per 30 minutes)
